LESSON: CARE FOR

Grade: PP2
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: HEALTH
Topic 4.1: Care For

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Care For. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we brush PRACTICES Teeth strand, the learner should that destroy their teeth our teeth?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Care For means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya
3. practise Care For in clear steps
4. apply Care For in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CARE FOR
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Care For helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CARE FOR
Study Care For like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Care For means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Care For means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Care For means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Care For” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Care For means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Care For matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Care For in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Care For in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Care For in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Care For this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Care For in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Care For in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Care For in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Care For in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Care For” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Care For in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Care For is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Care For” around your school. (skill: explain what Care For means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Care For matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Care For this week. (skill: practise Care For in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Care For” around your school. (skill: apply Care For in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Care For to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Care For means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Care For in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Care For from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Care For: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Care For?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we brush PRACTICES Teeth strand, the learner should that destroy their teeth our teeth?
2. When do we brush (5 Lessons) a) tell the dangers of appropriate teeth brushing our teeth?
3. What do we use to destroy teeth, • Learners could be guided in news telling rush our teeth?
4. How do we brush destroy teeth, • Learners sing songs and recite poems on our teeth?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Care For means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Care For means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Care For from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
